ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monetaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-20 to R.561-24 (UBO register), implemented by Loi n. 2016-1691 (Sapin II) of 9 December 2016 and Decret n. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017, as amended by Decret n. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020; transposing EU Directive 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive 2018/843 (AMLD5); Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cash controls; Code de commerce Articles L.123-53 and A.123-2 for the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, officers, directors and UBOs against: (a) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions File (CFSP lists), (b) UN Security Council consolidated lists (including ISIL/Al-Qaida and Taliban sanctions), (c) OFAC SDN list where USD payment rails (Swift LC, TT Wire) are used, (d) French national freezing measures via the French Ministry of Economy and Finance (FCPI) list, (e) PEP databases in line with FATF Recommendation 12 and AMLD4 Article 3(9); enhanced due diligence is triggered for individuals or entities residing in or sourcing from high-risk third countries listed by FATF and EU Delegated Regulation 2016/1675; continuous monitoring is required by the registering counsel and the onboarding French bank.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_threshold_basis: Direct and indirect holding of more than 25% of share capital or voting rights, or control by other means (CMF Article L.561-2-2); in the absence of an identified natural person, senior management officers are notified as UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalites d'Entreprise operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) database (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate filings and articles of association must be drafted in French (Code de commerce Article L.123-1-2). The SAS name may comprise any Latin-script denomination, mark or fantasy name; non-Latin or ideographic brands must be transliterated and/or accompanied by a French or Latin-script equivalent for registration. The name must not be likely to create confusion with an earlier registered company or a protected trademark in the national RNE database; the official name is registered exactly as filed without separate transliteration step.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Financement / Credit / Societe de financement (regulated terms requiring ministerial or ACPR approval)
Mutuelle / Caisse (regulated insurance or mutual terms)
France / Francaise / Paris (may be refused where it misleadingly suggests official endorsement)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no standalone pre-incorporation name reservation; name protection accrues upon effective registration in the RNE. If the INPI Guichet Unique rejects the incorporation filing because the chosen name is confusingly similar to an earlier entity or violates a prohibited token, counsel must: (1) obtain from INPI the written rejection grounds (decision de refus d'immatriculation); (2) within two months from notification, file a motion to rectify the name and resubmit the complete incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique; (3) where the name dispute involves a third party's prior rights, initiate adversarial proceedings before the Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) under Code de commerce L.123-1 et seq. and the general law of unfair competition (Code civil Articles 1240-1241), or file for cancellation of the prior conflicting trademark with INPI; (4) in parallel, conduct a full RNE and INPI trademark search and secure availability of the desired domain names; appeal of an INPI administrative refusal may alternatively be pursued before the Paris Court of Appeal within the applicable statutory time limits. Practical SOP requires pre-filing clearance via data.inpi.fr and consultation of national and EU trademark databases (TMview) before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: administrative domiciliation of the registered office (siege social) is allowed under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-167 through an authorized domiciliation company for a maximum of five years, renewable, without requiring the transfer of production substance. However, the industrial quick-freezing factory must have its own distinct physical facility in France, including cold-chain infrastructure, and must hold the separate sanitary approval (agrement sanitaire CEE) under Regulation (EC) 853/2004 and the French hygiene orders (arrete of 21 December 2009, as amended); a virtual office is therefore acceptable only as the administrative seat, never as the approved production premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 75% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Departemental Directorate for the Protection of Populations (DDPP) and DGCCRF within the first 12 months of operation, due to the frozen-food category-3 processing activity and the mandatory EU sanitary approval regime; additional unannounced cold-chain temperature and hygiene audits are routine after first approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-9 and R. 123-1 et seq. for company formation and registration, and Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 for the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Commercial and Companies Registry (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS), maintained by the relevant commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce); filings are submitted through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online company-formation filing (formalité de création) through the INPI Guichet unique, resulting in registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés and issuance of a Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a SAS; capital may be set at EUR 1. Cash contributions must be paid up by at least 50% upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash funds must be deposited before registration with an authorized bank, notary, or the Caisse des dépôts et consignations, and are released after registration. In-kind contributions must generally be fully contributed at incorporation; a contribution auditor may be required unless the statutory exemption conditions are met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the executed articles of association and acknowledge receipt of the required initial cash contributions evidenced by the deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the Company adopt the registered office at [full French address], subject to receipt of satisfactory proof of occupancy. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President (Président) of the Company, with authority to represent it in accordance with law and the articles of association, and that [name] be appointed [other officer, if applicable]. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to complete registration formalities, obtain the Company’s Kbis extract, and take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm name, registered office, and SAS governance terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises; INPI name-search services; competent RCS registry for the proposed registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed name for availability and third-party rights. Secure a French registered-office address and documentary evidence of the right to use it. Agree the share capital, share allocation, President, any other officers, and any required governance provisions. The SAS articles must identify the President and set out its governance arrangements.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business description
Registered-office evidence, such as a lease, domiciliation agreement, or proof of premises
Shareholder and beneficial-owner information
Draft articles of association
Identification and contact details of proposed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or conflicts with prior rights, amend it and repeat clearance. If office evidence is insufficient, provide an acceptable occupancy or domiciliation document before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute articles and deposit cash capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, French notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations for the capital deposit; shareholders for execution of the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and execute the articles of association. Open a temporary capital-deposit account and pay in at least 50% of cash subscriptions. Obtain the certificate of deposit for the registration filing. Execute documents electronically or in wet ink; notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS articles, but foreign-language or foreign-executed supporting documents may require certified translation, apostille, or legalization as applicable.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of association
Share subscription and payment details
Shareholder identity documents and, for corporate shareholders, current registry evidence and representative authority
Deposit certificate for cash capital
Contribution auditor report or documented basis for exemption, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary rejects the file, cure identity, source-of-funds, or corporate-authority deficiencies and obtain a corrected deposit certificate. If an in-kind contribution requires valuation, appoint a contribution auditor and revise the articles and filing package accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized journal of legal notices (journal d’annonces légales) in the département of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory formation notice with the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President details, and RCS registration location. Obtain the publication certificate and retain the published notice.
required_dossiers: Formation notice containing required statutory particulars
Executed articles or verified company particulars
Payment details for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused or details are inaccurate, correct the notice and obtain a replacement certificate before submitting the registration formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit company registration and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises, electronically routed to the competent RCS registry and relevant authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company-formation formalité online, upload the signed articles and supporting evidence, disclose beneficial owners through the applicable declaration, and pay the registry and beneficial-owner filing charges. The stated USD amount is an approximate conversion of standard French registry charges; the payable EUR amount and any additional charges must be confirmed in the portal at filing.
required_dossiers: Executed articles of association
Capital-deposit certificate
Registered-office evidence
Publication certificate for the legal notice
President’s identity document and signed non-conviction and filiation declaration, where required
Beneficial-owner information and supporting ownership chart
Corporate shareholder registry extracts and representative authority, if applicable
Signed power of attorney, if filing through an authorized representative
Required translations, apostilles, or legalizations for foreign documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI portal and respond within the stated deadline to any request for correction or additional evidence. Correct inconsistencies in the articles, beneficial-owner disclosure, identity records, or registered-office proof and resubmit the requested items; escalate registry refusals through the applicable review or appeal procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique; French tax administration (Direction générale des finances publiques); relevant bank and social-security authorities, as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, then complete the permanent bank-account conversion and deposit release. Maintain statutory accounting and corporate records, register share movements, and complete applicable tax and employer registrations. Confirm the company’s tax regime and VAT position with the tax administration.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET notices
Final articles and first board or shareholder resolutions
Capital-deposit evidence
Bank account opening and beneficial-owner records
Tax and VAT registration information
Employer registration documents, if hiring personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct discrepancies in the Kbis or registration data through the INPI formalities process. Provide outstanding bank, tax, or employer documentation promptly and suspend regulated operations until all required registrations and approvals are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent Prefect and the departmental Directorate for the Protection of Populations (Direction départementale de la protection des populations, DDPP) for food-safety oversight; the relevant regional Directorate for the Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement, DREAL) and Prefect for ICPE environmental permitting, as applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food-establishment registration and, where applicable, sanitary approval (agrément sanitaire) for handling products of animal origin under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Regulation (EC) No 853/2004; any applicable ICPE declaration, registration, or environmental authorization under the French Environmental Code.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique), with examination by the competent environmental authority and DREAL where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and capacity-dependent. Screen the facility against the current ICPE nomenclature, including applicable food-processing headings such as rubriques 2220 and 2221. The applicable regime may be declaration, registration, or authorization; an environmental impact assessment is required only where the applicable statutory screening thresholds and project characteristics trigger it. No blanket EIA exemption or full-report classification can be determined without capacity, process, location, and emissions data.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain the applicable ICPE order and local discharge authorization before commissioning. Meet the site-specific limits for wastewater flow, temperature, pH, suspended solids, organic load, and other regulated pollutants; comply with applicable municipal sewer acceptance conditions and water-police requirements. Control refrigerant leakage, combustion emissions, odours, and volatile organic compounds where relevant. Segregate, store, trace, and transfer animal by-products and other waste through authorized channels under applicable EU and French rules. Numeric limits depend on the applicable ICPE regime, permit, receiving system, and local orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, obtain any required building and planning approvals and comply with French fire-safety and workplace rules. Where the premises qualify as an establishment open to the public (ERP), obtain the applicable fire-safety and accessibility approvals and opening authorization. For industrial premises, document fire-risk controls, emergency access, evacuation, electrical and equipment safety, and any structural or floor-load requirements for freezers, racking, and machinery. Complete required occupational-risk assessments, including the single risk-assessment document (DUERP), staff training, and workplace-health obligations. Any additional fire or structural clearance is site- and classification-dependent.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident entities such as SAS obtain SIREN/SIRET identifiers and VAT number (FR followed by 11 digits) directly upon incorporation via the guichet unique portal. Foreign entities with French operations register as non-residents to secure statutory tax identification numbers and comply with withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available. Classification fixed by legal form (SAS). Hybrid mismatch provisions under ATAD Directive apply for cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing (e-facturation) for B2B transactions via France's national platform; API connectivity to tax authorities required for digital stamping and clearance compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU or services provided to non-EU customers, requiring proof of actual export and non-EU destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of non-EU payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties of 80% of evaded VAT plus interest for fraudulent zero-rating claims; retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits if export proof not maintained or provided during audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), 31 Rue Croix des Petits Champs, 75001 Paris — Direction Générale de la Stabilité Financière et des Opérations, in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; exercises Eurosystem delegated powers from the European Central Bank (ECB) and administers balance-of-payments statistics, cross-border capital monitoring, and foreign-exchange operational oversight under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier, CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility of the euro, consistent with Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. There are no quantitative convertibility limits, no foreign-exchange permits, and no blocking or prior authorisation for ordinary trade payments, dividends, or loan servicing. The euro is freely deliverable in France; French resident companies may freely hold foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) and settle in any currency via authorised credit institutions. Profit remittance by the SAS to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted at the exchange-control level; the operative hurdles are documentary and fiscal only: (i) a corporate distribution resolution supported by distributable reserves evidenced in audited accounts; (ii) French withholding tax of 25% (12.8% for non-resident individuals), reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the EU parent holds at least 10% of capital for at least 24 months, or to lower treaty rates (e.g., France-Germany treaty 0% at 10%+ shareholding); and (iii) presentation of the DGFiP tax regularity certificate (attestation de régularité fiscale) for larger dividend flows. All cross-border transfers are reported by the authorised intermediary bank to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics under CMF Articles R152-1 to R152-3; the company itself is not required to file a separate FX declaration for ordinary payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France abolished all mandatory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation deadlines, and conversion ratios by Law No. 90-1098. A French exporting SAS may retain 100% of its export receipts in foreign-currency accounts or convert them at market rates, with no statutory conversion band, no surrender timeline, and no minimum repatriation percentage. The only residual obligations are informational: (i) the French receiving bank records export receipts in the monthly Banque de France balance-of-payments transmission (single DEMO statistical file), using the appropriate current-account motif code; and (ii) physical cross-border transport of cash or bearer monetary instruments equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 must be declared by the traveller under EU Regulation 2018/1672 and the French CMF Article R152-3 — this is a carrier-level customs declaration, not a treasury obligation. No export licence or foreign-currency repatriation certificate is required for frozen food products (ISIC 1074).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre pour Dépôt de Capital) and Operational EUR / USD / CNH Multi-Currency Accounts
Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR / USD Accounts with Corporate Trade Finance Desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Accounts, including dedicated Agri-Food Industry relationship banking

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR and Multi-Currency Accounts; Capital Escrow available on a case-by-case basis

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC — Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale (CIC Banque CIC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account and Trade Finance Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium overall — High for EUR collection and low-value operational payments, Low for cross-border trade finance, documentary letters of credit, and FX hedging. Legal constraints: French and passported European EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business) are licensed under CMF Article L525-1 and PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366); they may provide payment accounts, card acquiring, SEPA/SWIFT payment initiation, and FX conversion at market rates through partner banks. They cannot issue, advise, or confirm documentary credits (MT700/MT710), cannot act as the authorised intermediary for Banque de France balance-of-payments declarations, cannot provide credit or negative balances beyond permitted intra-day arrangements, and are not accepted as depositary for regulatory capital escrow for share subscriptions. For the SAS frozen-food factory, an EMI is strictly complementary and must be linked to a Tier-1 bank account for LC settlement, correspondent USD clearing, and OTC forex contracts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for foreign directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). For a newly incorporated SAS whose shareholders are non-residents, French Tier-1 banks apply customer due diligence under CMF Articles L561-5 and L561-6 and the ACPR risk-based approach: the legal representative (Président) must attend an in-branch interview with the compliance officer presenting original passport or EU eID; each UBO must be identified in person at least once before account activation. Remote video onboarding is available only for simple deposit accounts at certain regulated neobanks and does not cover capital escrow or trade-finance lines. Where the President cannot travel, the bank will accept a notarised power of attorney granting signature authority to an in-country resident manager, but the UBO identification interview cannot be delegated and must be completed before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resident in a non-EEA jurisdiction subject to FATF enhanced monitoring or a country with opacity in corporate ownership records (e.g., high-risk third-country classification).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing of the shareholder(s); notarised shareholder register and chain-of-title documents; UBO declaration (formulaire Cerfa n° 11661*02) filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; professional banker's references from two regulated credit institutions in the shareholder's jurisdiction; clear organisational chart; and independent name-screening results from reputable media and sanctions databases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial capital escrow deposit or subsequent capital increases, particularly where the SAS has a very low nominal capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the subscribing shareholder's account; executed bulletin de souscription d'actions (share subscription form); evidence of the actual payment of funds from the shareholder account to the escrow account; audited annual financial statements or sworn net-worth statements of the subscribing shareholder; tax residence certificates proving lawful origin; and intercompany loan agreements where capital is contributed via shareholder current accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch or patterned same-day in-and-out transfers across EUR, USD, and CNH without underlying commercial documentation (potential trade-based money laundering indicator).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction dossier per shipment: sales and purchase contracts, pro-forma and final invoices, packing lists, transport documents (CMR, Bill of Lading, Air Waybill), French customs declarations (DAU), customs clearance receipts, warehouse receipts, and weight/count reconciliation tables; the ISIC 1074 frozen-food processing sector is classified as low AML risk, so full documentation normally downgrades the alert.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment instructions to suppliers or collection from buyers routed through third-party payment aggregators or offshore non-EEA jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficiary due-diligence forms with extracted commercial-registry data for each counterparty; sanctions and PEP screening results; written representation of commercial relationship; express restriction in the treasury mandate limiting payments to the contractual counterparty named in the underlying shipping documents; and clean correspondent-bank references for the creditor banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of non-bank channels (e-money institutions or digital-asset/stablecoin settlement) visible in proposed treasury flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate treasury policy restricting payment rails exclusively to ACPR-licensed credit institutions; complete transaction listings from any EMI with matched underlying invoices; and written confirmation that no cryptocurrency or stablecoin settlement is used for trade payments or payroll.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: non-resident shareholder issues a SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer from its own bank to the SAS capital escrow account at the French Tier-1 authorised intermediary, quoting in Field 70 'Subscription to share capital / capital increase of FR SAS' and in Field 72 the shareholder reference. The French receiving bank assigns the applicable Banque de France balance-of-payments motif code for inward direct investment in equity (category 'Investissements directs — titres de participation') in its DEMO statistical filing. No prior ministerial authorisation is required for the frozen-food manufacturing sector (ISIC 1074) under CMF Article L151-3, as the activity does not fall on the strategic-sector list. Verification pack released after compliance review: (i) certified or notarised statuts incorporating the capital amount; (ii) bulletin de souscription d'actions; (iii) minutes of the extraordinary general meeting resolving the capital increase; (iv) updated registre des mouvements de titres; (v) UBO declaration; and (vi) proof that the funds were received in cleared money from the shareholder's own account, without set-off, compensation, or third-party on-behalf payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury clearing rails: (A) SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfer / open-account settlement of raw-material imports (flour, shrimp, pork, seasonings) and SME export collections in EUR, USD, GBP, or CNH; EUR settlement clears via TARGET2 (T2) for large-value payments or via SEPA Credit Transfer in ISO 20022 pain.001 for EEA EUR payments below T2 thresholds; USD clears via Fedwire/CHIPS; CNH clears via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System). (B) SWIFT MT700 (issue) / MT710 (confirmation) documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 for structured trade settlement; the French bank issues import LCs in favour of raw-material suppliers and advises/confirms export LCs received from buyers of the frozen dim sum products. (C) SWIFT MT400 documentary collection for clean collections where LC terms are not required. The factory should maintain a revolving LC line and cash collateral or guarantee facility with the Tier-1 bank, and must ensure all outbound payment instructions include invoice numbers, transport references, and HS/ISIC codes for customs and statistical coherence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Permissible — Outright FX Forward (Change à Terme): OTC contract with any ACPR-licensed credit institution under an ISDA 2002 or FBF 1996 Master Agreement; no statutory underlying-transaction test applies to a French commercial SAS, and trades are subject to EMIR transaction reporting and internal treasury mandate limits.

Permissible — Cross-Currency Swap (Swap de Devises): permitted for EUR/USD and EUR/CNH exposure management, documented under an ISDA/CSA master agreement; where a financial counterparty is involved, mandatory margin exchange applies under EMIR uncleared-margin rules (VM/IM with UMR obligations) and transactions must be reported to an EU-registered trade repository.

Permissible with caveat — Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF): not a market-standard instrument for EUR because the euro is fully convertible and deliverable; NDFs may be booked exceptionally to hedge non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., onshore CNY, RUB, BRL) via an authorised French credit institution settling in EUR in the offshore market, with the resulting position reflected in the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration. For Chinese renminbi exposure, a deliverable CNH (offshore yuan) forward or swap is the preferred permitted alternative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Approval of Financial Statements and Result Allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (General Assembly or written decision for SAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain approval renders accounts unusable for distributions; the court may order a meeting at the request of any shareholder; no direct state fine, but the president risks civil liability; company strike-off if combined with non-filing over two years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Filing of Financial Statements at the Trade Register (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS - Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval, and in any case no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end (31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal injunction by the registrar; after two years of omission the company may be administratively struck off; the legal representative may be fined up to EUR 7,500 (legal entity) and an additional EUR 15,000 under the Commercial Code for obstructing controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership (Confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (integrated in the annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit; within 15 days of any change if occurring during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO register is a criminal infringement of the French Monetary and Financial Code; penalties up to EUR 7,500 for individuals and EUR 37,500 for legal entities, with possible imprisonment of six months for the operating director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse fiscale n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: second business day after 3 May of the following year; for a non-calendar year-end: second business day after the end of the 3rd month following the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic surcharge of the assessed tax, plus 0.20% monthly interest; deliberate neglect may increase the penalty to 40% and void carry-forward tax losses; failure to file may also attract a fixed fine of EUR 150 for missing schedules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: At least two of three thresholds must be exceeded at the balance sheet date to require an independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes): balance sheet total > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average payroll > 50 employees. If the SAS is a subsidiary in a group or holds corporate shares, other group-thresholds may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared in accordance with French GAAP (PCG - Plan Comptable Général), including the rules of the Autorité des Normes Comptables. IFRS is permissible only for consolidated financial statements of listed groups and is not required for a privately-owned French SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual deposit of the financial statements with the RCS includes a specific UBO validation field. The company's signatory certifies that the beneficial ownership declarations on file remain accurate. If a share transfer or other ownership change occurred, a separate modification of the beneficial owners must be filed with the same registrar within 15 days following the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (and share transfers, if any, under the SAS Bylaws)
Register of Directors and Corporate Governance Decisions (register of societary decisions)
Minute Book (procès-verbaux of shareholders' meetings and board resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 – US$1,100 per year (typical French registered-office or virtual office domiciliation cost)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000 – US$25,000 per audit cycle (if mandatory threshold exceeded; range for a mid-size frozen-food manufacturing SAS)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of specified innovation expenses; possible exemption for Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) within EI conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited (indefinite, annual offset cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit above such cap)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Cerfa 2065) corporate income tax return together with annexed schedules 2050 through 2059, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional workspace or TéléEDI/EDI-TDFC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate tax instalments (acomptes d'IS) payable quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the financial year-end; for calendar-year entities filing by 30 April of the following year. Electronic filing mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of the financial year (Résultat de l'exercice) before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment (PE) report only the net profit attributable to the French PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments and deductions (déductions extra-comptables, retraitements).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate common expenses on an auditable and consistent apportionment basis reflecting PE activity; keep supporting records.
Enter the net taxable base subject to the standard corporate income tax rate after all lawful deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating losses carried forward and used in the year (déficits reportables imputés).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the French PE may be deducted; no foreign branch losses unless allowed under domestic PE rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (crédits d'impôt) such as CIR/CII.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claimable only for expenses actually attributed to the French PE and producing income taxable in France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% penalty on the net assessed tax plus late interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.20% per month. After formal notice, a further 40% or 80% penalty may apply for failure to file or for inaccurate returns; individual fines up to EUR 10,000 may be imposed by the tax court.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower treaty rate, the beneficial owner must, before payment, deliver a French tax residence certificate issued by the foreign tax authority to the French payer (Form 5000 or equivalent). The payer then reduces withholding at source. If the 25% statutory WHT has been deducted, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the French tax authorities (Service des impôts des particuliers) within the limitation period, ordinarily by 31 December of the second year following the year of receipt. EU/EEA parent companies may benefit from the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption where a 5% shareholding is held for at least two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 25%, treaty rates commonly reduced to between 0% and 10% depending on the DTA. Interest: statutory WHT 0% for arm’s-length non-resident lenders outside non-cooperative jurisdictions, except interest received by an established foreign PE or from a non-transparent loan; 25% statutory WHT applies to payments to entities resident in non-cooperative states, with treaty reductions to 0%-10% where applicable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (aggregate group turnover or gross assets) triggering mandatory Local File and Master File; Country-by-Country reporting applies above EUR 750,000,000 consolidated annual revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the OECD BEPS substance requirements through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (abus de droit, Art. 64 LPF) and the principle of substance over form. A French SAS must demonstrate actual personnel, premises, decision-making, and commercial risk in France; artificial arrangements without economic substance are disregarded and treaty benefits denied under the Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of taxable profit, use of fictitious invoices, or concealment of intra-group revenue in foreign shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal reassessment plus 80% penalty for intentional tax fraud and late interest at 0.20% per month. Criminal conviction under Art. 1741 CGI may result in up to five years’ imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, or seven years / EUR 1,000,000 in aggravated circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who initiate, approve, or knowingly benefit from evasion are personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; travel bans, asset forfeiture, and imprisonment may be imposed. In extreme cases, the corporate veil is pierced to attach liability to management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SAS with no commercial substance, e.g., routing manufacturing or purchasing transactions through an entity without employees, premises, or real control over risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of the artificial structure under GAAR (abus de droit) with an 80% penalty; denial of treaty benefits; reassessment of profits attributable to the substance-less entity; possible administrative fines up to EUR 750,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally required to restore sums distributed or trapped in shell structures, and may face commercial court disqualification or civil restitution orders; if fraud is proved, criminal liability attaches.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce contemporaneous TP documentation despite meeting the EUR 400 million threshold, or refusal to answer an official request under Article L13 AA of the French Tax Procedures Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic reassessment of intra-group prices with 40% penalty for gross negligence and late interest at 0.20%; non-response after formal notice incurs an administrative fine of up to EUR 10,000 plus potential criminal sanctions for obstructing tax control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable where they knowingly signed false or misleading TP documentation; penalties may be lifted against directors who personalise the corporate fault under the 'faute lourde' doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments above the statutory limit (EUR 1,000 for business-to-business) or executing transactions with sanctioned entities through opaque financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to 5% of the unlawful cash amount; criminal prosecution for money laundering carrying up to EUR 150,000 fine and imprisonment; increased penalties under the Monetary and Financial Code for repeated or organised infractions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate cash laundering face imprisonment up to seven years, EPC/ACM restrictions, travel bans, and disqualification from corporate management; compliance officers may also be sanctioned.
